assertions.notes: A was booked at 18:00 (S1) on 2026-10-22 while availability offered 28 times. POST /manage/modify {localMin:1140} -> 200 and the manage view showed 19:00; a second POST {localMin:1215} -> 200 and the view showed 20:15 (startAt 2026-10-23T00:15Z, endAt 01:30Z). Each modify released the old occupancy (active=0) and inserted the new active one on G9-2 (sqlite). Engine assignment observable: at 19:00 the slot proposal was G9-Area-Strict before, G4-Area while A occupied it, and G9-Area-Strict again after A moved on (freed). The freed 18:00 time was rebooked by a different guest (H, rsv_445b603f...) with 201. Modifying to a time with no feasible seating returned 409 {"error":"slot_unavailable","alternatives":{sameDay:6,otherDates:6}} for 16:00 (between services) and 22:00 (past last seating for the 75-min turn); the follow-up GET /manage showed the booking still at 20:15 (I6 unchanged).
assertions.limitations: (1) No genuinely capacity-exhausted time exists to construct on the seeded date: each party size has 10+ feasible table assignments and this group may not write pacing/settings rows, so the 409 path was exercised with times that have no engine slot rather than a fully-booked valid slot. (2) 'Freed/consumed' was verified at the engine-assignment level (slot proposal area + occupancy rows), not as a time vanishing from the list: because the day has spare tables, the freed time is re-offered through another table (G4-Area) rather than the same best-fit table; the freed best-fit table (G9-2) returned to the 19:00 proposal after the second modify.

assertions.notes: With large_party_mode=request and online_party_max=8, POST /reservations/requests (Idempotency-Key) for party 12 on 2026-10-22 returned 201 with status 'requested' (DB row pending_approval) and request_deadline set. Replaying the identical key+body returned 201 with the same reservation id and confirmation code. request_holds_capacity=1: the pending request D held G10-T11 for its window (active occupancy row 18:30-19:30 local) and the operator booking-sheet availability for party 12 at 20:30 changed its suggested table from tbl_084ea289 (G10-T11) to tbl_71be1db7 (G10-T12) while a second request F was pending, returning to G10-T11 after F was declined. Approve: POST /operator/reservations/book/reservations/<D>/approve -> 200 {ok:true}; the guest manage view then showed status 'booked' (time 18:30, party 12) and sqlite status 'booked'. Decline: POST .../<E>/decline -> 200 {ok:true}; sqlite status 'declined', cancel_reason recorded, and E's occupancy on G10-T11 was released (active=0); same for F.
assertions.limitations: The contract's 'availability for that window shrinks' could not be observed through the public guest availability endpoint: with the seeded wide-open day every publicly offered party size (<=8) still has other 8-fit tables free, and the held 1-12 table is never the public best-fit, so GET /reservations/availability?partySize=8 was byte-identical before/after D (22 slots, same area proposals). The capacity hold and its release were instead evidenced by the active occupancy row for the request window, the operator booking-sheet suggested-table change/revert, and the release on decline. This is a dataset observability limit, not an API defect; no assertion outcome depended on it. Out-of-scope observation: the book-scope operator token (no read:reservation_guest:any) still receives full guest phone/email in the approve/decline response detail and the day feed (serializeGuestRow always emits phoneE164/emailNorm; only notes/tags/allergy notes are gated by canReadGuestSensitive) - whether that is intended (hosts need contact info) is for the parent to judge.
